body.statement:
Every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) satisfies the conditional orthogonality
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)\right\}W\mid z_0\right]=0
\]
for every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable random variable \(W\).  Hence every design event \(E\in\mathcal X\) with \(0<\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)<1\) has the same conditional treated mean on \(E\) and \(E^c\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} removes the former common-design-shock obstruction.  This repair does not by itself determine an exact asymptotic minimax constant: there are admissible scalar fixed class parameters and, for every positive \(N,T,n_1\), two laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\) having the same joint law of \((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) and the same target \(\tau(z_0)=0\), while
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered product experiment.
body.justification: The theorem records exactly what the repaired sampling model rules out and why that repair is not an exact-constant calculation.
body.gap: Exact constants for the remaining centered optimal-recovery product experiment are left to the fresh open question.
body.consumer: The model-class audit can remove the obsolete negative answer without overstating what centering proves.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), a cohort \(s\), and a unit \(i\), and put
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
Membership, \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}, and \texttt{ass:consistency} make this conditional mean finite.  By \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=0.                            \tag{5}
\]
Let \(W\) be bounded and \(\mathcal X\)-measurable.  Then \((B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\) is integrable, and \(W\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The pull-out and tower properties of conditional expectation applied to (5) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\mid z_0]
 &=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 \mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right]\\
 &=0.
\end{aligned}                                                                                \tag{6}
\]
This is the asserted conditional orthogonality.

Now take \(E\in\mathcal X\) and write \(p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)\).  Substituting \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) into (6) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=\mu_{si}p_E.                          \tag{7}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division of (7) by \(p_E\), using the definition of conditional expectation on an event, yields
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E]=\mu_{si}.                                     \tag{8}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E^c]=\mu_{si}                                    \tag{9}
\]
whenever \(p_E<1\).  Thus (8)--(9) hold simultaneously if \(0<p_E<1\).  The exclusion of the former common-design-shock experiment is exactly \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}.

It remains to prove that this centering repair does not itself fix the centered event-noise constant.  For every positive \(N,T,n_1\), choose the admissible scalar fixed parameters
\[
 S=1,
 \quad \pi_1=1,
 \quad H=0,
 \quad p=d=1,
 \quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,
 \quad B=L=1,
 \quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with arbitrary fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  The identity \(d=p(H+1)=1\) and all displayed parameter ranges are satisfied.

On a product probability space, let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\), \((\xi_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \Pr(\xi_j=1)=\Pr(\xi_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \Pr(\varepsilon_i=1)=\Pr(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12.
\]
Define the untreated regression, training responses, and donor scores by
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j.                                                                          \tag{10}
\]
For every event unit put \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level},
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.                                                                           \tag{11}
\]
Under \(P^{(0)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\).  Under \(P^{(1)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In both laws impose \texttt{ass:consistency} by defining \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  The buy-and-hold formula then gives
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12
 \quad\text{under }P^{(0)},
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }P^{(1)}.                                                                  \tag{12}
\]
All constructed returns lie in \((-1,\infty)\), because the smallest possible return is \(-1/2\).

We verify every member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\).  Equations (10)--(12) give
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\]
so \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds with \(B=1\).  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\), every positive-order derivative equal to zero, and Holder seminorm zero.  Hence \(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), as required by \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_X(x)=1\quad(0\le x\le1),                                                                  \tag{13}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-path} and \texttt{ass:design-density}.

Conditional on the complete design array, every training outcome in (10) is deterministic.  Under \(P^{(0)}\), the event outcomes are deterministic; under \(P^{(1)}\), unit \(i\)'s event history depends only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Independence of the \(\varepsilon_i\)'s therefore proves \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} while leaving no restriction beyond the stated conditional independence across units.  The calendar blocks in (10) are independent over \(t\), so their beta-mixing coefficients satisfy
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,                                                                               \tag{14}
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Declaring each \(X_{1t}\) in (10) directly observed verifies \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Equation (10) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Q_{1ti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(X_{1t}).                                                                                \tag{15}
\]
Under either law, (12), independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\), and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].                                               \tag{16}
\]
Thus both clauses of \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} hold.

For the clarified donor-versus-joint-panel factorization, define
\[
 \mathcal D=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}
 =\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T},(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^{n_1}).
\]
By (10), every \(Q_{1ti}\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal X\), while by (12) every event outcome is either constant or measurable with respect to \(\sigma((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1})\).  Hence \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}\subseteq\sigma((X_{1t})_t,(\varepsilon_i)_i)\).  Conversely, \(\mathcal D\subseteq\sigma((\xi_j)_j)\).  Mutual independence of the three primitive arrays therefore yields
\[
 \mathcal D\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}\mid z_0,                  \tag{17}
\]
where conditioning on \(z_0=1/2\) is conditioning on a constant.  Equation (17) is exactly the clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}; it factors the donors from the entire joint panel and places no additional restriction on dependence within a unit history.

By (10), conditional on the fixed \(z_0=1/2\), the donor scores are independent and identically distributed and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0)=1.                                                 \tag{18}
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Since \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), (18) proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Finally,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 |\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[|\xi_j|^4]
 =1
 =B^4,                                                                                        \tag{19}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} while retaining the full scalar covariance.

Equation (11) and the definition of \(m_1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(z_0),                                                                                  \tag{20}
\]
so \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} holds.  Consistency was imposed before (12).  We have therefore verified every member property listed in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, and hence
\[
 P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}.
\]
In particular, neither law uses a class-wide lower local-modulus condition.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is the same under \(P^{(0)}\) and \(P^{(1)}\) by (10) and the common product construction.  By \texttt{def:target}, (11)--(12), and the zero mean of a Rademacher variable,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \tau_{P^{(0)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(0)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]=0,\\
 \tau_{P^{(1)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(1)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac14\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0.
\end{aligned}                                                                                \tag{21}
\]
Nevertheless, (12) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) yield
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)
 =\frac1{16}.                                                                                \tag{22}
\]
Thus the centered class permits both event-noise constants while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target fixed.  Equations (5)--(9) prove the asserted orthogonality and eventwise mean invariance, while (10)--(22) give the explicit two-law certificate under the clarified donor-versus-joint-panel factorization.  Therefore excluding the invalid common-design-shock witness is logically distinct from calculating a sharp minimax constant for the remaining centered product experiment.
